MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JULY 16, 2018

An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 6:00 p.m. at the Highridge Park, 29035 Highridge Road, Rolling Hills Estates, California by
CHAIR ROMANELLI.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Chair Romanelli, Persichina, Pope, Retz
  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Portugal, Wroan
  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 18, 2018 –
  NO QUORUM

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  “BUTCHER PARK” COMMUNITY MEETING UPDATE

  Baxter Miller, BMLA, provided an overview of the community meeting (held on June 20, 2018)
  and the preliminary proposed design for the new park at Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos
  Verdes Drive East.

  In response to a question by CHAIR ROMANELLI, Community Services Director Clark stated that
  “Butcher Park” is not the name of the park. Naming of the park will be decided at a later time.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked about the walk path. Mr. Miller stated that the walk path was not
  included in this preliminary design.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about parking spaces. Mr. Miller stated that the property
  is too small for parking. Suggestions for visitor parking are, the nature center or along Palos Verdes
  Drive East at Dapplegray Park. Mr. Miller added that this will be a pocket park mostly used by
  nearby residents.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she was at the community meeting and those more invested
   in this project are those who are in the neighborhood and will walk there.

  Paul Marlon, Resident of Hitching Post Drive, asked about the purpose of the park and expressed
  his concern about traffic.

  Robert Day, Resident of Pony Lane, expressed concern with accessibility. Community Services
  Director Clark stated that there is street parking that may be used.

  Sally Kensey, Resident of Pony Lane, expressed concern with getting to the park since it may be
  difficult for small children to walk there from surrounding residences.

  Ryan McCormick, Resident of Dapplegray neighborhood, inquired about fencing. Mr. Miller stated
  that there is consideration of installing a 3-rail fence.

  Mr. McCormick also stated that having only one entrance would be helpful with supervising
  children, and asked about consideration in relocating the entrance away from traffic. He also asked
  about the play structures that are incorporated in the design and asked if consideration could be
  given to incorporating an obstacle course into the design.

  Scott Combs, Resident of Montecillo neighborhood, inquired about installing a barrier in the event
  of an accident at the intersection. Mr. Miller stated placing boulders may be an option and that the
  monument sign may also serve as a barrier. Mr. Miller’s colleague stated that there are also trees
  around the park that may also serve as a barrier.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there are large boulders throughout the city that can
  be placed at the park as barriers.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI thanked the residents for their input and BMLA for the project update.

  B.  NATURE CENTER MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT ADDENDUM

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary of the staff report on the nature
  center management agreement and stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission make a recommendation to the City Council to approved a fourth amendment to the
  agreement with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy for the Nature Center contract
  Naturalist services through June 30, 2020.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Ms. Vona stated that the 15%
  increase will provide funding to maintain adequate staff during operational hours. Ms. Vona also
  noted that the PVP Land Conservancy’s costs to provide Naturalist services are increasing
  annually.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE A
  FOURTH AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT WITH THE PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY FOR THE NATURE CENTER COTRACT
  NATURALIST SERVICES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2020.

  Ayes:  CHAIR ROMANELLI, POPE, PERSICHINA, RETZ
  Noes:

Park and Activities Commission  Page 2 of 5
Minutes, July 16, 2018
   Absent: PORTUGAL, WROAN
  Abstain:

  C.  PROPOSED HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL PROJECT

  Community Services Director Clark provided background on the previous mural project and
  provided a brief summary on the proposed project.

  Marianna Desalles provided samples of the artwork and an overview of the structures where the
  artwork could be placed throughout the park.

  A brief discussion ensued and the Park and Activities Commission agreed that they are in favor of
  the project and asked that Ms. Desalles bring in renderings showing what the murals will look like
  on the various buildings.

  D.  TEMPORARY STREET BANNERS

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief summary on this request.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA to,

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF PERMANENT PLYWOOD BOARDS PAINTED
  WHITE AND GREEN IN THE TEMPORARY BANNER SITES THROUGOUT THE CITY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  E.  CITY CELEBRATION/MUSIC FESTIVAL SUBCOMITTEE UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated that direction from the City Council is to keep the City
  Celebration and the Musical Festival as separate events.

  The Park and Activities Commission expressed their disappointment on the outcome and the
  manner in which the collaboration between the city and Betty’s foundation ended.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there will be collaboration with the City and Betty’s
  Foundation only on the marketing side. A coupon will be sent along with the “Remember the Music”
  festival flyer which will be good for various activities at the City Celebration event at the Empty
  Saddle Club.

  Community Services Director Clark added that if the music festival will be held at Ernie Howlett
  Park, Betty’s Foundation has decided to choose a date which will not interfere with the City
  Celebration event.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that he got a report from COMMISSIONER RETZ
  regarding damage to the 3-rail fence at Club View Drive.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there will be any re-assignment of parks. Community Services
  Director Clark stated that he will add this to the August agenda.

Park and Activities Commission  Page 3 of 5
Minutes, July 16, 2018
   9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TENNIS TOURNAMENT SHIFTS (sign-up sheet)

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he may have a conflict. COMMISSIONER POPE stated that
  she will volunteer for the Saturday morning shift.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JUNE 26, 2018

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JULY 5, 2018

  C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2018

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved to receive and file items 10-A through 10-C

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  COMMISSIONER ROLES DURING CITYWIDE DISASTERS – SEPTEMBER 17TH

  Community Services Director Clark stated that Alexa Davis, Assistant to the City Manager and
  Jessica Slawson, Administrative Analyst will attend the meeting to provide information on
  Commissioner’s roles during citywide disasters.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting to the Highridge Park park tour at 7:06 p.m.

  Items noted for repair or replacement:

  •  Restrooms – repair of exterior and suggestion for better lighting
  •  Drinking fountain may be turned the wrong way (ADA compliance)
  •  Concrete borders may be removed and installed with a more durable material
  •  Spray weeds on walking path
  •  Cap broken on control valve (found past 2nd drinking fountain)
  •  Flashing missing on storage at baseball field
  •  West side of park may need sprinklers repaired
  •  Left field and foul ball area – irrigation
  •  Purple plum trees in bad shape
  •  Sand bags left on field
  •  (2) illegal drains from homes off of horse trail
  •  Fencing planks hanging off (east side of park)
  •  Siding on maintenance storage garage

  12.  ADJOURNMENT TO PARK TOURS OF CHANDLER, PEPPERWOOD, ROCKBLUFF, AND
  SILVER SPUR PARKS AT 6:00 P.M. ON AUGUST 20, 2018

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the next Park and Activities meeting will not be a
  park tour due to construction in the scheduled area. The meeting will be a regular meeting held in
  the City Hall Council Chamber.
